text:
If you were hoping for a calm sunset walk, tonight's got other plans. It's still warm and sticky out there, mid-80s with that mostly clear sky starting to give way, but showers and thunderstorms move in as soon as this evening, likely between 7 and 8, with the real activity picking up after dark. Low around 70, and up to half an inch of rain possible, so keep an eye on the sky if you're out late. The lake's calm through this evening, waves a foot or less, but I wouldn't linger past dark with thunder in the mix.

Saturday carries the same pattern: showers and storms likely in the morning, tapering to just a chance by afternoon, with partly sunny breaks in between. High near 85, feeling closer to 90 with the humidity. The European model is notably wetter than the American one for tomorrow, so don't be surprised if it rains more than a passing shower suggests. Good air quality both days. If you've got outdoor plans Saturday, morning's the wet window; afternoon looks like your better bet, though I'd still keep the rain jacket handy.

week.blurb: Sunny and warm to 87, but showers and thunderstorms roll in after dark with a soaking half inch possible.
Morning storms linger into the afternoon, high near 85, and I'd bet on wetter than the official 50 percent.
Any leftover morning showers clear out fast, leaving a mostly sunny Sunday near 86.
Warm and mostly sunny to 85, then storms build late and turn likely overnight as the front arrives.
The front crosses through with scattered showers and thunderstorms and a cooler high near 82.
High pressure settles in, drier and more comfortable near 81 with just isolated shower chances.
Trending toward another round of likely showers and storms, with highs easing back to near 79.
